questions: Should the subsequence be strictly increasing by value only, or must it also be strictly increasing by index (which is already implied by being a subsequence of the prefix)?
If there are multiple strictly increasing subsequences satisfying the constraints, do we need the maximum possible length or any valid length?
Are duplicate values allowed in the subsequence if they appear at different indices but have the same value, given 'strictly increasing'?
Does 'elements at most X_i' refer to the values of the elements in the subsequence, or to the indices of the elements?
Is the subsequence required to be selected from the first R_i elements exactly, or can it be any subsequence of the full array but only considering elements up to index R_i?
If no subsequence exists (e.g., all elements in prefix exceed X_i, but guarantee says X_i >= min, so at least one element <= X_i exists), should we return 0 or 1?
Does 'strictly increasing' apply to the values only, or must the indices also be strictly increasing (which is inherent in subsequence definition)?
Should the subsequence be contiguous or not? (Already clarified as not necessarily contiguous.)
